jobs.title: Chief of Staff (Executive Office) and VP of Strategy & Operations
jobs.description:
Flex is a growth-stage, NYC headquartered FinTech company that is creating the best rent payment experience. It’s hard to believe that it’s 2026 and paying rent on time is expensive, inflexible, and difficult. We’re here to change that! Flex enables our users to pay rent throughout the month on a schedule that better fits their finances and budget. Our mission is to empower as many renters as possible with flexibility over their most significant recurring expense. After deliberately keeping a stealth profile as we built up unprecedented investor support and an enthusiastic user base, we are looking for motivated individuals to help us keep our mission growing. Will you be a part of the team?

About the Role

The Strategy & Operations team is the "API" through which company strategy, operating rigor, and ways of working are translated into execution across Flex. As Chief of Staff and VP of Strategy, you will serve as a senior partner to the CEO and COO, owning the central Strategy & Operations (S&O) team, shaping enterprise strategy, refining our operating model, and driving the hardest problems in the company to resolution.

This role reports directly to the CEO and sits at the intersection of the Executive Office and the S&O team. It requires someone who can work the system, not just the project, and who is willing to force the conversations that need to happen, even when that's uncomfortable.

This is a hybrid position with on-site expectations of 3 days per week in our New York Headquarters. For candidates outside of the NY/NJ/SF area, you may be eligible for our relocation assistance program.

What You'll Do

1. Chief of Staff to the Executive Office The Executive Office sets the pace and tone for how Flex operates. Your job is to make it run at its best: decisions made with clarity and speed, communications that reflect the quality of the thinking behind them, and the CEO and COO free to focus on what only they can do. This means:

- Serving as a trusted thought partner and sounding board to both executives, helping pressure-test decisions before they're made and accelerating alignment when speed matters

- Owning the highest-stakes communications: board materials, company-wide messaging, and external engagements, ensuring every artifact reflects the quality and clarity of their thinking

- Managing the rhythm of the Executive Office: preparing for critical meetings, ensuring follow-through on key commitments, and keeping the most important decisions from stalling

- Leading special projects on behalf of the Executive Office, stepping into high-priority, time-sensitive workstreams that require senior judgment and a trusted hand

- Holding a high bar for the quality of the top team: proactively surfacing what's working and what isn't, delivering honest upward feedback, and creating the conditions for the executive team to operate at its best

2. Enterprise Strategy & Cross-Functional Initiatives You will personally own the highest-stakes strategic work at Flex, the questions and initiatives that don't fit neatly inside any one division or function. This includes:

- Leading major cross-departmental initiatives end-to-end, from problem definition through outcome delivery

- Shaping enterprise-level strategy on market expansion, organizational design, and long-range planning

- Serving as a trusted advisor to the CEO and COO with the credibility to drive decisions forward and push back when needed

- Stepping in where needed, whether that's board deck preparation, executive communications, or high-priority cross-functional support

3. Team Standard-Bearer You will own the health, performance, and trajectory of the S&O team, a small, high-powered cohort operating across Flex's most critical domains. This means:

- Setting and upholding standards of excellence in analytical rigor, communication quality, and operational discipline

- Leading recruiting with a clear, consistent bar for what great looks like at every level

- Owning career development, structured feedback, and coaching

- Building the team as a true cohort with shared identity, operating norms, and mutual accountability

What You'll Bring

- 15+ years of professional experience with a track record spanning management consulting and/or senior S&O, Biz Ops, or Chief of Staff roles at high-growth companies

- A first-principles problem solver: when the map runs out, you build a new one. You don't need a clean brief to do exceptional work, and you've been recognized for figuring it out in ambiguous, high-friction environments

- Resilient and comfortable with ambiguity: you structure messy problems, move quickly, and revise as you learn, without losing your footing

- Proven team leadership: you've built, developed, and scaled high-performing teams, and take genuine ownership over the growth of the people around you

- Exceptional ability to work the system, not just the project: you understand organizational dynamics, know how to move people, and can make things happen without formal authority

- Skilled at influencing up: you bring the right conversations to leadership, push back when needed, and earn trust through substance, not title

- High horsepower, low ego: you're as comfortable rolling up your sleeves on an urgent deliverable as you are shaping a long-range strategy

- Outstanding written and verbal communication: clear in writing, confident in the room, and able to translate complexity into crisp recommendations and decisions

- Demonstrated AI fluency: you actively leverage AI tools to accelerate analysis, improve team workflows, and drive better decisions, and you set the standard for how your team uses them

- Sound commercial judgment: you understand how businesses work, spot risk and opportunity quickly, and make decisions that hold up under scrutiny

- Strong quantitative reasoning: whether through financial modeling or analytical problem solving, you're comfortable turning complex data into clear, defensible recommendations

- Exceptional emotional intelligence: you know how to read a room, build trust with executives, and show up as both a partner and a coach (even with the CEO)

- NYC-based and available to work from Flex's Union Square office 3+ days per week

Nice to Have

- Experience in fintech, consumer lending, or payments

- Familiarity with the operating rhythms of a late-stage growth company

Compensation

Flex takes a market-based approach to pay, ensuring compensation is commensurate with a candidate's experience and our internal leveling guidelines. For candidates located in our Tier 1 (NYC/Bay Area) markets, the base salary pay range for this role is below. Flex utilizes a geographic pay differential based on a cost of labor index. If you are located outside of the cities listed below, your starting pay will be adjusted to align with the market conditions of your specific geographic zone. Please speak with your recruiter for additional information regarding the specific range for your location.

Tier 1 (NYC/Bay Area)
$320,000 — $400,000 USD

Life at Flex

We understand that it takes a diverse team of highly intelligent, curious, determined, empathetic, and self aware people to grow a successful company. Our HQ is located in New York City, but we have employees located throughout the US, Australia, Canada and South America. We are growing quickly, but deliberately, with a focus on building an inclusive culture. Our dynamic team has incredible perspectives to share, just as we know you do, and we take great pride in being an equal opportunity workplace.

Offices

Roles posted in New York, San Francisco, and Salt Lake City are hybrid positions with on-site expectations of 2-3 days per week in our local offices. For candidates outside of these areas, you may be eligible for our relocation assistance program.

Benefits

For full-time U.S. employees we offer:

- Competitive medical, dental, and vision

- Company equity

- 401(k) plan with company match

- Unlimited paid time off + 13 company paid holidays

- Parental leave

- Free Flex subscription

For full-time non-U.S. employees, we offer:

- Competitive compensation + company equity

- Unlimited PTO

About the Role

This role is the tip of the spear for Flex's largest, most complex, and most strategically important deals. As we expand into new verticals and new enterprise relationships, we need a technical sales leader who can do more than present a demo. You'll own the solution layer of the sales process end-to-end: translating complex customer environments into winning proposals, building conviction with technical and executive stakeholders alike, ensuring that what we promise is something we can actually deliver, and working with Product & Engineering teams to ensure customer needs are a key input to internal roadmaps.

This is the founding hire for Flex's New Verticals Solution Engineering function. You'll start as a hands-on, high-impact operator with Director-level scope, and you'll build the foundation the function scales on: the playbooks, the demo environments, the discovery frameworks, and the hiring plan. As new vertical pipeline matures, you will recruit, hire, and lead a team of Solution Engineers, with a defined path to formal people leadership of the SE organization. We are looking for someone who wants to earn that mandate by winning deals first, then scale themselves through a team.

What You'll Do

- Own the technical sale on our largest, most complex deals: Lead solution engineering activity for Flex's highest-priority opportunities in new verticals, from discovery and scoping through proof-of-concept, technical validation, and close.

- Build trust with technical and executive buyers: Engage executive stakeholders at prospective partners. Translate Flex's capabilities into business outcomes that resonate at the board level and in the weeds equally.

- Architect solutions that win and scale: Deeply understand each prospect's technology, data environment, and operational requirements. Design integration and deployment approaches that are commercially compelling and technically sound, working shoulder-to-shoulder with Flex Engineering to validate feasibility before we commit.

- Drive proof-of-concept and pilot execution: Lead structured POCs and pilots that de-risk the decision for the customer and accelerate time-to-close. Define success criteria, coordinate Product and Engineering resources, manage execution, and turn results into momentum.

- Partner with Sales to shape deal strategy: Function as a true co-owner of the deal alongside the Account Executive, contributing to account strategy, surfacing risks, and helping design the right commercial and technical structure.

- Build the New Verticals SE function, not just the playbook: Document discovery frameworks, integration patterns, objection handling, and competitive differentiation as we enter each new vertical. Create reusable assets (demo environments, solution briefs, RFP libraries) that raise the floor for future deals and make every SE hire behind you productive faster.

- Define and execute the SE hiring plan: Build the business case for headcount as vertical pipeline scales. Own the hiring bar: write role profiles, design the interview process, recruit, and onboard the first Solution Engineers on the team.

- Grow into leading the team: As the function scales, transition from founding IC to player-coach to people leader. Set the operating rhythm, coach SEs on deal execution, and own quality across the SE motion in new verticals.

- Partner deeply with Product and Engineering: Operate as the connective tissue between the field and the build. Synthesize technical feedback from deals into structured, prioritized product input, align Engineering on customer requirements during active cycles, and influence the roadmap by making the business case for what new verticals require.

- Shape how Flex shows up in market: Partner with Marketing and Business Development on technical content, event presence, and thought leadership that builds Flex's credibility with enterprise buyers in new segments.

Key Qualifications

- 10+ years of experience in pre-sales, solutions engineering, or technical sales, with at least 4 years operating in a senior or lead capacity on complex enterprise deals.

- Demonstrated track record closing large, multi-stakeholder, technically complex sales cycles, ideally in FinTech, PropTech, payments, or adjacent SaaS/infrastructure categories.

- Experience building or scaling an SE or technical pre-sales function: hiring SEs, developing talent, and establishing the processes and assets a team runs on. Formal people management experience is a strong plus; demonstrated readiness and ambition to lead a team is required.

- Exceptional ability to engage and build credibility with C-suite and VP-level technical buyers; equally comfortable in a boardroom and in a technical architecture review.

- Deep fluency in enterprise integration patterns (APIs, webhooks, data pipelines, ERP/property management system ecosystems) with the ability to get hands-on when needed.

- Strong commercial instincts: ability to shape deal structure, anticipate objections, and understand how technical decisions affect economics on both sides of the table.

- Experience operating in a greenfield or early-stage vertical context. Comfortable building process, playbooks, and teams from scratch rather than inheriting them.

- Track record of functioning as a cross-functional bridge: influencing product roadmaps, aligning engineering teams to customer requirements, and partnering closely with marketing and BD.

- Outstanding written and verbal communication; the ability to distill complex technical and financial concepts into clear, persuasive narratives for diverse audiences.

- High ownership orientation: someone who treats the customer's success as their own, moves urgently without needing to be told to, and multiplies their impact through the people they hire and develop.

- FinTech, real estate technology, or multi-sided marketplace experience is a strong plus.

jobs.description:

It’s hard to believe that it’s 2026 and paying rent on time is expensive, inflexible, and difficult. We’re here to change that! Our mission is to empower as many renters as possible with flexibility over their most significant recurring expense. About the Role

Flex is looking for an experienced contractor to support our Revenue Strategy & Operations team on sales compensation. Most of the work is building our commissions capitalization approach with Accounting. You'll take the plans we have today and turn them into a defensible, repeatable capitalization schedule that holds up in an audit. You will size the price and you'll also help model new compensation plans and pick up analytics requests from Revenue leadership. The role is about 30 hours a week, and the hours can flex up or down for the right person.

What you'll do

Commissions capitalization

- Partner with Accounting to apply ASC 340-40 to Flex's commission plans.

- Build the calculations that show recoverability: link commission dollars to the units and revenue they generated, and work out the capitalizable portion when payouts exceed the related revenue.

- Recommend and document amortization periods and methods, such as expected customer life or portfolio approaches.

- Build a repeatable monthly or quarterly capitalization and amortization schedule that runs off the existing comp run outputs. Hand it off with documentation that a non-author can run.

- Prepare audit-ready support and documentation of methodology.

- Point out plan-design changes that would make more of the commission spend clearly capitalizable.

New plan design support

- Model proposed plan changes for the 2027 plans: quotas, pay curves, accelerators, caps and SPIFFs.

- Estimate plan cost against OTE and SPIFF budgets, and run scenario analysis for leadership.

- Draft plan documents and rollout materials alongside Alex.

Key Qualifications

- 6-8+ years in sales compensation, revenue or technical accounting, or FP&A, with direct exposure to commission plans.

- Hands-on experience implementing ASC 606 / 340-40 commission capitalization, not just maintaining someone else's schedule.

- Advanced Excel/Google Sheets modeling. Precise, organized and comfortable being audited.

- Ability to explain accounting mechanics clearly to non-accountants and comp mechanics to Accounting.

- Self-directed. Can deliver with light oversight on a part-time schedule.

- SQL (or AI-assisted querying) and experience with Snowflake, Sigma and Salesforce data.

- Background at a comp consultancy (Alexander Group, SBI, Simon-Kucher) or Big 4 audit or advisory.

- Experience building comp plans 0 to 1 in a high-growth environment.

What Success Looks Like

- First 30 days: inventory of current plans with a capitalization classification for each payout type, capitalization mechanism calculated for AE and AMs

- By Q4 close: capitalization and amortization schedule live and tied to comp run outputs, with documentation ready for audit.

- Ongoing: plan scenario models delivered on time for 2027 planning, and analytics requests turned around within agreed SLAs.

Compensation
